title: Mitchison (1980, 1981) Proc. R. Soc. B / Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B & Feugier, Mochizuki & Iwasa (2005) J. Theor. Biol. — With-the-Flux Auxin Canalization, Sachs Wound Bypass Regeneration, and Carrier-Allocated Open vs Closed Leaf Venation Networks
organism: Pisum sativum & Arabidopsis thaliana (dicot leaf lamina and stem vascular strands)

primary_sources.citation: Mitchison (1980) Proc. R. Soc. Lond. B 207(1166):79-109
primary_sources.role: Facilitated diffusion canalization model dD_ij/dt = alpha*phi_ij^p + beta - gamma*D_ij proving that linear feedback (p <= 1) yields diffuse flow whereas quadratic feedback (p = 2) triggers winner-take-all symmetry breaking into 1-cell-wide vascular strands where concentration drops inside the canalized vein (S_vein < S_parenchyma)

primary_sources.citation: Mitchison (1981) Phil. Trans. R. Soc. Lond. B 295(1078):461-471
primary_sources.role: Polar auxin transport canalization with directed membrane carrier permeabilities P_ij evolving with net flux phi_ij, explaining basipetal polarity and Sachs wound bypass strand regeneration

primary_sources.citation: Feugier, Mochizuki & Iwasa (2005) J. Theor. Biol. 236(3):366-375
primary_sources.role: Coupled auxin flux and PIN1 efflux carrier allocation dynamics on a 2D leaf lamina comparing open hierarchical branching trees (unbounded/non-saturating carrier feedback) vs closed-areole venation loops (saturating carrier allocation with distributed lamina synthesis)
Experimental demonstration of auxin-driven vascular strand canalization and C-shaped bypass regeneration around a transverse stem incision in Pisum sativum
Comparative evaluation of facilitated diffusion vs polar transport canalization and open vs closed loop formation in dicot leaf venation

specimen_metadata.author: Wikimedia Commons contributor (de-ghosted cleared dicot leaf skeleton)
specimen_metadata.description: Cleared dicotyledonous leaf venation skeleton against a black background showing the primary midrib, pinnate secondary veins branching at ~54.5 deg, and reticulate tertiary/quaternary closed areole loops.
